title: a-run-that-fails-to-run-leaves-a-trail-and-counts
author: cc
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(a_failed_run_is_counted) -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: each rehearsal record written with ran:false (rehearse() writes it through the artifact door); the probe reads CairnCommons/rehearsals/ on the beat that already runs
watchme.enough: 10 failed-to-run records on live tickets, each counted by passes_since_clean and none read by the lane as clean or gaps
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: failed passes seen, counted, misread
watchme.nexus: the rehearsal machine's own record of what a pass costs
watchme.consumer: CC at session open; codemother, owner of the care of the code

intention: Every run of a runner leaves a trail entry: a run that fails to run is recorded as a run and counts toward the runner's caps, but is never recorded as a verdict. Rehearsal is the first case; a sieve makes it standard for every declared runner.
why: Akien, 2026-09-29: "shouldn't a rehsersal pass be counted like a testing pass?" / "nice. then that should be standard practice?" / "yes, cast it after BUILDME". Measured the same day on cd8096f9eeca: two rehearsal passes refused (exit 2, reader failed the schema three times) wrote no record and did not count toward PASS_CAP — ~20 minutes of runs the record says never happened (Law 7).
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are permanent in records of truth); Law 3 (the pass cap measures passes and was undercounting); Law 4 (the standard becomes a sieve).
how: Catch ReaderFailed in rehearse() and write a ran:false record; passes_since_clean counts it; the lane is untouched because only a clean pass writes the ticket's rehearsal pointer. A build_inspector sieve reds a declared runner whose failure-to-run path writes no trail.

falsifier.proves_green: GREEN when a rehearsal pass with a failing reader writes a record under CairnCommons/rehearsals/ carrying ran:false and the refusal text, passes_since_clean counts it, the ticket's rehearsal pointer is not moved by it, and the sieve reds a declared runner whose failure path writes nothing.
falsifier.wrong_intent: WRONG INTENT if counting failures makes the cap fire on outages rather than on thin tickets — measured by cap questions whose five passes were all ran:false.

links.what: sibling: the tester's half — a timeout is not a red (no verdict); this ticket: it is still a run (a trail entry, counted)
where it was measured: two refused passes, no records

decisions.text: D1 WHERE IT FAILS TODAY: rehearsal.py read_tree raises ReaderFailed after RETRIES_PER_READ+1 (=3) attempts; rehearse() does not catch it, so no record is written and __main__ exits 2. The reader's own subprocess timeout (claude_reader, timeout=300) surfaces inside read_tree as a reader error and ends in the same raise.

D2 THE FAILED RECORD: rehearse() catches ReaderFailed and writes, through the same door.write call and the same file naming as a normal record (rehearsals/<ticket>-<stamp>.json, verb 'rehearse'), a record with keys ticket, record, at, pass, ran (false), clean (false), why (the ReaderFailed text), ticket_sha256_at_read, reads (the trees that did pass, possibly empty), gaps ([]), meta (model, attempts, cost_usd, duration_ms, rendered_chars, by). A normal record gains ran: true. The CLI still exits 2 and prints the record path.
D3 COUNTING: passes_since_clean (rehearsal.py:417) counts a ran:false record like any unclean record — it increments n and the reset rules are unchanged.

D4 THE LANE IS UNTOUCHED: the_ticket_rehearses_clean reads only the ticket's rehearsal pointer, and only a clean pass writes that pointer (rehearse, clean branch), so a ran:false record can never satisfy or move it. standing() is unchanged.

D5 THE SIEVE: build_inspector gains sieve 'a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail' over a declared runner list in cairn/machines/build_inspector/sieves/runners_leave_trails.json: each row {runner, module, failure, trail} names the exception or path that means 'did not run' and where its trail lands. v1 rows: rehearsal (ReaderFailed → CairnCommons/rehearsals/) and tester (proof timeout → ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0/*.TesterDevice.run_proof.json). The sieve reds a row whose module's failure path reaches exit without a write — measured by calling it with an injected failing reader/proof in a scratch root, never by reading code.

D6 THE PROOF: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_failed_run_is_counted.py, prove-first (written and run RED before the build): a scratch commons with one ticket; a reader that always returns nothing; teeth — (1) rehearse raises nothing past the catch and a ran:false record exists; (2) passes_since_clean went from 0 to 1; (3) the ticket's rehearsal pointer is unchanged; (4) the sieve reds a planted runner whose failure writes nothing and greens rehearsal. Every output marked testing.

Falsifier clause (1) is added by this line: the ticket's falsifier carries proves_green and no proves_red, so proof_coverage reads no clause; clause 1 IS the proves_green text (a failing reader's pass writes a ran:false record carrying the refusal, passes_since_clean counts it, the pointer is not moved, and the sieve reds a declared runner whose failure path writes nothing). The proof keys PROVES {'ba4166fe51c4': {'1': 'test_a_failed_pass_writes_a_ran_false_record_carrying_the_refusal'}}; the other three teeth run beside it as guards. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

ReaderFailed gains an attempts attribute: read_tree sets it to the attempts list it accumulated before raising, so the ran:false record's meta.attempts carries every failed attempt (RETRIES_PER_READ+1 of them for the read that failed, plus those of reads that passed before it). Its docstring is rewritten to the new contract: a record IS written, with ran:false. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
decisions.step: unlisted: the attempts on the failed record

decisions.text: _open_the_question takes the standing gaps from the latest record whose ran is not false; with none, gaps is []. A ran:false record carries gaps [] by D2, and naming no gaps because the reader failed would hide the last real ones. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
decisions.step: unlisted: the cap question reads only ran records

decisions.text: cairn rehearse's one-pass branch: when the returned record has ran false it prints to stderr 'reader failed on pass <n> over <ticket>: <why> — <record>' and returns 2; the Refused handler is unchanged for every other refusal. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

test_rehearsal.py's tooth test_a_schema_failure_is_re_read_and_a_reader_that_never_satisfies_it_writes_nothing pins the contract this ticket replaces; it is renamed test_a_schema_failure_is_re_read_and_a_reader_that_never_satisfies_it_writes_a_ran_false_record (its PROVES 'reread' entry with it), and its second half asserts rehearse returns ran false, exactly one record is in rehearsals/, and the journal is ['rehearse']. Its re-read half is untouched. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

build_inspector gains declared_runners() (reads cairn/machines/build_inspector/sieves/runners_leave_trails.json, a list of rows {runner, component, failure, trail, drive}) and sieve a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail(row, comp_dir, *, runners=None), registered in SIEVES. For each declared row whose component equals the census row's, it makes a scratch dir (cairn.tools.scratch, prefix 'runner-trail-testing-'), runs the row's drive argv with {scratch} replaced, cwd the repo, timeout 180, and globs trail under the scratch dir; no match (or a drive that cannot be run) is one finding naming runner, failure, trail and the drive's exit. A component with no row yields []. RULE 1: the drive is each runner's own public CLI verb, never an import of its code. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

rehearsal: `python3 -m cairn.machines.rehearsal --drive-a-failed-run <scratch>` builds a scratch commons under <scratch>/CairnCommons with one testing ticket and runs rehearse with a reader that returns nothing; trail 'CairnCommons/rehearsals/*.json'. tester: `bin/cairn test --drive-a-failed-run <scratch>` writes a testing proof that sleeps 30s under <scratch>, points a TesterDevice's diagnostic roots at {repo, commons, instance: <scratch>/.cairn} and runs run_proof(sink='none', timeout=2); trail '.cairn/logs/tester/0/*.TesterDevice.run_proof.json'. Each verb is added to its charter's public_interface. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof is written and on disk, red-first: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_failed_run_is_counted.py, a scratch commons with one testing ticket and a reader that always returns nothing; TEETH runs four in order — (1) the ran:false record carrying the refusal (PROVES clause 1, D7), (2) passes_since_clean 0 -> 1, (3) the pointer and ticket bytes unmoved, (4) the sieve reds a planted runner whose drive is `true` and greens every declared row. Measured 2026-10-11 before the build: RED 0/4 — tooth 1 'the pass raised past the catch: ReaderFailed(read 1 ...)', tooth 2 (0, 0), tooth 3 no record, tooth 4 no sieve. The tester drive was tried by hand in a scratch root the same day: red 'timed out after 2s' in 4.6s, its trail .cairn/logs/tester/0/<stamp>.TesterDevice.run_proof.json under the scratch dir. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
